items: Run non-root: `USER` in the Dockerfile, not a run-time patch.
`--read-only` rootfs plus a tmpfs for the writable paths.
`--cap-drop=ALL`, then add back only what actually breaks.
Secrets in tmpfs or a manager — env vars leak via `docker inspect`.
Desktop bind mounts remap ownership (Windows drives often show 0777).
So permission bugs first surface on the Linux deploy.
Test ownership on Linux before you trust it.
One default network per project; services without `networks:` join it.
Services resolve each other by service name. No `links` needed.
Extra networks: top-level `networks:` plus a per-service list — which drops `default` unless you list it.
Unquoted `22:22` is base-60 in YAML 1.1 (it reads 1342) — quote ports.
`external: true` means it exists — don't create or delete it.

caption.text: Your container can't be reached and your database just vanished — a network namespace gave it a private network, and its writable layer dies with the container. Part 4 of DOCKER NETWORKING & VOLUMES covers least privilege, the Compose default network, and the `ports:` and `volumes:` keys that mean different things in the same slot. Save it before the next Permission denied.
